findings.title: Portfolio drift exceeds tolerance in US equities and Canadian bonds
findings.detail: The portfolio is overweight in US equities by {{m:drift.US_EQUITY.pp}} and underweight in Canadian bonds by {{m:drift.CA_BONDS.pp}}. These drifts exceed the tolerance of {{m:cfg.drift_tolerance.pp}}, requiring rebalancing to maintain the balanced risk profile.

The non-registered account holds {{m:acct.NON_REG.value.cad}} in total, with {{m:alloc.CASH.pct}} of the total portfolio in cash, largely due to the bonus mentioned in CRM notes. Deploying this cash into underweight asset classes like Canadian bonds would reduce drift and align with the target allocation.
findings.title: Uninvested cash in non-registered account contributes to portfolio drift

findings.detail: The US-listed fund USEQ is currently held in the TFSA. Under simplified educational rules, US-listed foreign-dividend paying securities may be subject to withholding taxes in a TFSA that are not recoverable, making them less tax-efficient in this account type compared to others.
findings.title: US-listed security held in TFSA
Unused TFSA room with taxable interest in non-registered account
findings.detail: There is {{m:tax.tfsa_room.cad}} of unused TFSA contribution room, while {{m:tax.nonreg_interest.cad}} in interest-generating assets is held in the non-registered account. Moving interest-bearing assets to the TFSA can shelter that income from taxation.

findings.title: Interest-income assets held in non-registered account
findings.detail: The client holds {{m:tax.nonreg_interest.cad}} in interest-income assets within the non-registered account. Interest income is generally taxed at the client's full marginal rate, making it less tax-efficient than other types of investment income in non-registered accounts.

The portfolio's current volatility of {{m:risk.vol.pct}} is within the {{m:risk.vol_band_max.pct}} limit for a balanced profile. This aligns with the client's long-term horizon and low liquidity needs.
findings.title: Portfolio volatility is within suitability limits
Portfolio downside risk in equity bear market scenario
findings.detail: A simulated equity bear market scenario results in a potential loss of {{m:stress.equity_bear.cad}}, representing {{m:stress.equity_bear.pct}} of the total portfolio value. Given the client's age and long-term horizon, this downside exposure should be reviewed for comfort.

findings.title: No single-security concentration issues detected
findings.detail: No single security exceeds the concentration limit of {{m:conc.limit.pct}}, indicating a well-diversified portfolio structure.

US equity markets experienced significant growth, with the index returning {{m:mkt.us_equity_ytd.pct}} percent year to date. This performance, driven by technology sector gains, likely contributed to an overweight position in the client's US equity holdings.
findings.title: US equity growth drives portfolio drift

findings.detail: Canadian bond yields have trended lower, with the ten-year yield currently at {{m:mkt.ca_10y_yield.pct}} percent. This environment, coupled with a year-to-date return of {{m:mkt.ca_bond_ytd.pct}} percent for the Canadian bond index, has influenced the valuation of the fixed-income portion of the portfolio.
findings.title: Canadian bond market performance impacts fixed income allocation
